steps.title: Six first-time users, eleven tasks, one colour each
steps.line: The report’s colours become scores: green 5 down to black 1.
steps.caption: Researchers for GNOME’s design team watched six people who had never used GNOME, aged 21 to 47, try eleven tasks in test builds of Files 47. Their report colours each attempt from green, no difficulty, to black, unable to complete. To plot attempts as journeys, this page scores green 5 down to black 1.

steps.title: P1, the first four tasks: gave up on Undo
steps.line: Each marked task is a give-up, scored 1, the lowest.
steps.caption: One column per task, in session order; the higher the face, the easier it went. Red marks a give-up: Undo is in the Main Menu, which none of those who quit opened.
steps.picture: User journey: 4 tasks, scored from 1 to 5, actor P1. Gave up: 4 Undo the move: score 1 of 5.

steps.title: P1, the next four tasks: no give-ups
steps.line: P1 finished all 4; the lowest score here is 2.
steps.caption: The report numbers tasks by topic; by the article’s list of the order, the list-view task 11 and the search task 10 came seventh and eighth. No one gave up on any of them; P1’s lowest score was 2, on the new folder.
steps.picture: User journey: 4 tasks, scored from 1 to 5, actor P1. New in this step: List view layout; Search; Experience curve: lowest 2 (11 New folder in list view), highest 5 (5 Change the sort order, 6 Grid view to list view); and 4 more.

steps.title: P1, the last three tasks: gave up on Open Item Location
steps.line: Each marked task is a give-up, scored 1, the lowest.

steps.title: All six gave up at least once, always in the menus
